entries.title: Basic Anatomy Review

testable_competencies.anatomy: Foundational ocular anatomy (globe, adnexa, orbit) that frames chapter content but is not independently tested.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Differential Diagnoses of Common Presentations (Overview)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Organizing differential table for vision loss/red eye/pain presentations frames the individual presentation units below but is not itself a distinct MCC objective.

testable_competencies.differential_framework: Organize common ophthalmic presentation differentials (vision loss, red eye, pain, floaters, flashes, photophobia, diplopia) by category.

entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: WEAK/indirect MCC evidence retained (rather than cleared to []) because the cited objective's scope genuinely touches this organizing topic, even though the evidence is not independently sufficient to support a DIRECT/COMPONENT classification for this framework-level content.
entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute, sudden loss of vision is the presentation-level match to MCC objective 115-1; the chapter's differential (retinal, vascular, optic-nerve, neurologic causes) directly frames this objective's diagnose-cause-severity-complications requirement.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Chapter's DDx table also covers gradual/progressive vision loss (cataract, glaucoma, AMD, diabetic retinopathy), matching 115-2.

testable_competencies.triage: Distinguish sudden painless (vascular/retinal emergency), sudden painful, and gradual/progressive vision loss, and identify which require same-day ophthalmology referral versus urgent stroke workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct presentation-level match: MCC objective 30 explicitly requires diagnosing the cause/severity/complications of eye redness and recognizing which conditions require urgent referral to prevent vision loss.

testable_competencies.triage: Differentiate benign red eye (subconjunctival hemorrhage, viral conjunctivitis) from vision-threatening causes (acute angle-closure glaucoma, scleritis, keratitis, uveitis, orbital cellulitis) requiring urgent referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Ocular pain substantially overlaps the red-eye differential (keratitis, scleritis, angle-closure glaucoma, uveitis all present with pain); no standalone MCC ocular-pain objective exists.

testable_competencies.triage: Localize pain (surface/foreign-body-type vs. deep/boring) to narrow the differential and identify red-flag features requiring urgent referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: New floaters, especially with flashes, can herald retinal detachment or vitreous hemorrhage -- an acute-vision-loss-risk presentation under 115-1.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize sudden shower of floaters +/- flashes/curtain field loss as requiring urgent same-day ophthalmology assessment to rule out retinal detachment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Photopsia is a classic warning symptom of posterior vitreous detachment or retinal tear/detachment, matching the acute-vision-loss-risk scope of 115-1.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize photopsia as a retinal-traction warning sign requiring dilated fundus exam to exclude retinal tear/detachment.

entries.title: Photophobia (Severe Light Sensitivity)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Photophobia commonly co-presents with corneal/anterior-segment inflammation captured under Eye redness (30), but is itself a non-specific symptom without a dedicated MCC objective; also overlaps migraine and meningismus, which are outside this chapter's scope.

testable_competencies.differential: Recognize photophobia as a nonspecific symptom of anterior-segment inflammation (keratitis, uveitis) versus non-ophthalmic causes (migraine, meningeal irritation).

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct presentation-level match: MCC objective 23 explicitly requires diagnosing the cause/severity of diplopia and determining whether true binocular diplopia (resolves with monocular occlusion) is present.

testable_competencies.triage: Distinguish monocular from binocular diplopia and recognize pupil-involving third-nerve palsy as a neurosurgical emergency requiring urgent imaging.

entries.title: Ocular Problems in the Contact Lens Wearer

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Contact-lens wear is a key risk factor the Eye redness objective's evidence base flags for urgent-referral corneal infection (microbial keratitis, especially Pseudomonas/Acanthamoeba).

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize contact-lens-associated red eye/pain as requiring urgent slit-lamp assessment to exclude microbial keratitis, and counsel on lens-hygiene risk factors.

entries.title: The Ocular Examination

testable_competencies.exam_technique: Perform and interpret the core bedside ocular examination: visual acuity, confrontation visual fields, pupil exam, extraocular movements, external/slit-lamp inspection, fluorescein staining, and intraocular pressure estimation -- the basic exam skills that underlie recognition of every presentation in this chapter.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Ocular Emergencies (Triage Overview)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This is a triage/overview list of true ophthalmic emergencies already individually evidenced under their own disease-specific units; retained at WEAK strength here only to flag the organizing 'requires same-day referral' competency itself.

testable_competencies.triage: Recognize the finite list of true ophthalmic emergencies (chemical burn, acute angle-closure glaucoma, central retinal artery occlusion, globe rupture/penetrating trauma, orbital compartment syndrome) that require immediate same-day action rather than routine referral.

entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: WEAK/indirect MCC evidence retained (rather than cleared to []) because the cited objective's scope genuinely touches this organizing topic, even though the evidence is not independently sufficient to support a DIRECT/COMPONENT classification for this triage-overview-level content, and the disease-specific evidence lives on the individual emergency units instead.
entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Optics (Refractive Errors and Correction Basics)

testable_competencies.refraction: Basic optics/refractive-error concepts (myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism, presbyopia) that frame chapter content; no dedicated MCC objective exists for refractive error itself.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Globe Displacement (Proptosis/Enophthalmos)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Proptosis is most commonly caused by thyroid eye disease, already evidenced under the Graves' ophthalmopathy unit; no dedicated MCC 'globe displacement' objective exists.

testable_competencies.differential: Differentiate proptosis (thyroid eye disease, orbital tumour, orbital cellulitis) from enophthalmos (blow-out fracture, orbital fat atrophy).

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No dedicated MCC 'cellulitis' objective exists (confirmed via search-mcc-objectives); orbital cellulitis presents with red eye plus vision-threatening/urgent-referral features, matching the urgent-referral scope of objective 30.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Orbital cellulitis frequently arises from sinus infection extension rather than trauma; WEAK cross-link retained only because periorbital soft-tissue infection shares assessment principles with the Trauma objective's complication-recognition scope.

testable_competencies.triage: Differentiate preseptal (eyelid-confined, afebrile, normal EOM/vision) from orbital cellulitis (proptosis, painful/restricted EOM, vision change, fever) -- orbital cellulitis is a true emergency requiring immediate IV antibiotics and imaging.

entries.title: Lacrimal Apparatus Disorders (Dry Eye, Epiphora, Dacryocystitis, Dacryoadenitis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Dacryocystitis can present as a painful, red, swollen medial-canthus mass overlapping the red-eye/periorbital-infection differential; dry eye and epiphora are common low-acuity complaints with no dedicated MCC objective.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize dacryocystitis (acute lacrimal-sac infection) as requiring antibiotic treatment and possible urgent referral, and distinguish it from the chronic, low-acuity dry-eye/epiphora spectrum.

entries.title: Lid Swelling and Inflammatory/Infectious Lid Lesions (Hordeolum, Chalazion, Blepharitis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Blepharitis is a classic chronic red-eye/lid-margin differential; hordeolum and chalazion are bread-and-butter primary-care lid presentations overlapping the same differential, though no dedicated MCC lid-lesion objective exists.

testable_competencies.recognition: Differentiate hordeolum (acute, painful, infectious) from chalazion (chronic, painless, granulomatous) and recognize blepharitis as a chronic lid-margin condition managed with lid hygiene.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Severe ptosis obstructing the visual axis (especially congenital, risking deprivation amblyopia) is the only member of this group with any vision-scope relevance; trichiasis/entropion/ectropion have no dedicated MCC objective.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize lid-malposition disorders (ptosis, entropion, ectropion, trichiasis) and identify acquired ptosis with pupil involvement as a red flag for third-nerve palsy or Horner syndrome requiring urgent neurologic workup.

entries.title: Xanthelasma

testable_competencies.association: Recognize xanthelasma as a cutaneous sign that may prompt lipid-panel screening; no dedicated MCC objective exists for this finding itself.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Conjunctivitis (viral/bacterial/allergic) is the single most common cause of red eye and the paradigm case for MCC objective 30's diagnose-cause-and-determine-urgency requirement.

testable_competencies.differential: Differentiate viral, bacterial, and allergic conjunctivitis by history/exam and recognize features (severe pain, photophobia, vision change, contact-lens wear) that mandate urgent referral rather than empiric treatment.

entries.title: Benign Conjunctival/Subconjunctival Lesions (Pinguecula, Pterygium, Subconjunctival Hemorrhage)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: These are the classic benign causes of a red eye that must be recognized and reassured rather than over-investigated, directly informing objective 30's severity/urgency triage.

testable_competencies.reassurance: Recognize subconjunctival hemorrhage, pinguecula, and pterygium as benign, self-limited or slow-growing causes of red eye/eye surface change not requiring urgent referral (absent red-flag features).

entries.title: Episcleritis versus Scleritis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Scleritis is a vision-threatening cause of red eye (often associated with systemic vasculitis/connective tissue disease) requiring urgent referral, versus benign self-limited episcleritis; no dedicated MCC sclera-specific objective exists.

testable_competencies.triage: Differentiate episcleritis (mild, self-limited, blanches with phenylephrine) from scleritis (severe boring pain, does not blanch, associated systemic autoimmune disease, vision-threatening, urgent referral).

entries.cross_discipline_note: Scleritis substantially overlaps Rheumatology's connective-tissue-disease/vasculitis objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-recognition angle only.

entries.title: Corneal Foreign Body and Corneal Abrasion

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Corneal foreign body/abrasion is a classic acute red-eye/eye-pain ER presentation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Corneal foreign body/abrasion is frequently a minor-trauma mechanism, weakly cross-linking to the general Trauma objective.

testable_competencies.management: Diagnose corneal foreign body/abrasion with fluorescein staining, exclude a retained intraocular/deep foreign body or infection, and recognize rust rings and organic-material mechanisms as needing referral.

entries.title: Recurrent Corneal Erosion

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Recurrent corneal erosion presents as recurrent painful red eye, usually following a prior abrasion; no dedicated MCC objective exists for this specific entity.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize recurrent corneal erosion (recurrent pain, often on waking, history of prior corneal injury) as distinct from a new abrasion.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Corneal ulcer/microbial keratitis is a vision-threatening cause of red eye requiring urgent ophthalmology referral, directly within objective 30's urgent-referral scope; especially relevant to contact-lens wearers (see unit 10).

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize corneal ulcer (white corneal infiltrate, severe pain, photophobia, contact-lens history) as a same-day ophthalmology emergency requiring culture and urgent topical antimicrobial therapy.

entries.title: Herpes Simplex Keratitis and Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both present as painful red eye with a vision-threatening infectious cause requiring urgent referral and antiviral therapy, matching objective 30's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize dendritic corneal ulceration (HSV keratitis, topical corticosteroids contraindicated) and Hutchinson's sign (nasociliary nerve involvement predicting ocular herpes zoster) as requiring urgent ophthalmology referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Infectious Diseases' herpesvirus objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-recognition/referral angle only.

entries.title: Keratoconus

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Progressive corneal ectasia causing chronic irregular-astigmatism vision loss; specialist (contact lens/corneal cross-linking/transplant) management dominates the source content.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize progressive, irregular astigmatism in a young patient as suggestive of keratoconus warranting ophthalmology referral.

entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: WEAK/indirect MCC evidence retained on this SPECIALIST_DETAIL unit (rather than cleared to []) because the cited objective's chronic-vision-loss scope genuinely touches the initial recognition step, even though specialist corneal management dominates the source content.
entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Corneal Signs of Systemic Disease (Arcus Senilis, Kayser-Fleischer Ring)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Kayser-Fleischer ring is a classic sign of Wilson disease (a genetic/metabolic condition); arcus senilis in a young patient prompts dyslipidemia screening. No dedicated MCC objective covers either finding directly.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize Kayser-Fleischer ring as a slit-lamp sign of Wilson disease and arcus senilis in a young patient as a prompt for lipid screening.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Kayser-Fleischer ring substantially overlaps Medical Genetics/Gastroenterology (Wilson disease) content; retained here in thin form for the exam-finding-recognition angle only.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cataract is the leading cause of gradual, chronic, painless vision loss worldwide, matching MCC objective 115-2's diagnose-cause-severity-complications scope directly.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize gradual painless vision loss with glare/haloes as consistent with cataract, and know the indication for surgical referral (visual-function impairment) versus observation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: PVD is the most common benign cause of new floaters/flashes (see units 6-7 above) but must be distinguished from retinal tear/detachment, within objective 115-1's diagnostic scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize PVD as usually benign but requiring dilated fundus exam to exclude a retinal tear.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Vitreous hemorrhage causes acute vision loss/floaters (commonly from proliferative diabetic retinopathy or retinal tear), within objective 115-1's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize sudden painless vision loss with vitreous hemorrhage (diabetic retinopathy, retinal tear) as requiring urgent ophthalmology referral to identify and treat the underlying cause.

entries.title: Endophthalmitis and Vitritis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Endophthalmitis is a true intraocular-infection ophthalmic emergency (post-surgical or endogenous) causing acute vision loss, within objective 115-1's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize post-intraocular-surgery/injection pain, redness, and vision loss as endophthalmitis until proven otherwise, requiring same-day ophthalmology emergency referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Infectious Diseases' intraocular-infection content; retained here in thin form for the ocular-emergency-recognition angle only.

entries.title: Retinal Artery Occlusion (Central/Branch)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CRAO is the paradigm cause of sudden, painless, profound vision loss and the clearest match to objective 115-1's diagnose-cause-severity-complications-and-initiate-management scope.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CRAO is a retinal-stroke equivalent requiring the same urgent stroke-protocol workup as objective 41 (amaurosis fugax/TIA), and shares its cardiovascular risk-factor evaluation.

testable_competencies.emergency: Recognize CRAO (sudden painless profound vision loss, cherry-red spot, afferent pupillary defect) as an ocular stroke equivalent requiring immediate ophthalmology/stroke-protocol activation.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps the Neurology/Emergency Medicine stroke-protocol objectives; retained here for the ocular-recognition angle.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: RVO causes acute-to-subacute painless vision loss, within objective 115-1's scope, though generally less time-critical than arterial occlusion.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize RVO (sudden painless vision loss, 'blood and thunder' fundus) and its association with hypertension, diabetes, and glaucoma, and initiate urgent ophthalmology referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Retinal detachment (curtain/veil vision loss, flashes, floaters) is one of the classic true ophthalmic emergencies and a direct match to objective 115-1's scope.

testable_competencies.emergency: Recognize the flashes/floaters/curtain-field-loss triad as retinal detachment requiring same-day ophthalmology referral, and distinguish rhegmatogenous from other detachment types.

entries.title: Retinitis Pigmentosa

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A chronic, progressive, inherited cause of vision loss (night blindness, tunnel vision); within objective 115-2's scope only at WEAK strength given its specialist-genetics-heavy management.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize progressive night blindness and peripheral (tunnel) visual field loss, especially with a family history, as suggestive of retinitis pigmentosa.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Medical Genetics' inherited-retinal-disease content; retained here in thin form for the ocular-recognition angle only.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: AMD is the leading cause of chronic central vision loss in older adults in the developed world, a direct and highly prevalent match to objective 115-2's scope.

testable_competencies.differential: Distinguish dry from wet (neovascular) AMD, recognize acute metamorphopsia/central scotoma in known AMD as a wet-conversion red flag requiring urgent referral for anti-VEGF therapy, and counsel on Amsler-grid self-monitoring.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Open-angle glaucoma is a leading cause of chronic, insidious, irreversible peripheral vision loss, matching objective 115-2's chronic-vision-loss scope.

testable_competencies.screening: Recognize open-angle glaucoma as asymptomatic until advanced (peripheral field loss), requiring periodic IOP/optic-disc screening in at-risk patients, and know that normal-tension glaucoma can progress despite normal IOP.

entries.title: Secondary Open-Angle Glaucoma

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A specialist-management-heavy subset of chronic glaucoma (steroid-induced, pigmentary, pseudoexfoliative, etc.); WEAK link to 115-2.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize steroid-response glaucoma as a risk of prolonged topical/systemic corticosteroid use requiring IOP monitoring.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute angle-closure glaucoma is a classic true ophthalmic emergency (painful red eye, fixed mid-dilated pupil, hazy cornea, nausea/vomiting), directly within objective 30's urgent-referral scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute angle-closure glaucoma causes acute vision loss and is equally a direct match to objective 115-1.

testable_competencies.emergency: Recognize acute angle-closure glaucoma (severe eye pain, red eye, headache, nausea/vomiting, fixed mid-dilated pupil, hazy 'steamy' cornea) as a same-day ophthalmic emergency requiring immediate IOP-lowering treatment and referral, and identify precipitants (dim light, anticholinergic/sympathomimetic drugs).

entries.title: Pupillary Examination and Abnormalities

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A pupil-involving third-nerve palsy (fixed dilated pupil plus diplopia/ptosis) is a neurosurgical emergency (compressive aneurysm) that shares evaluation with objective 23's diplopia scope.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Relative afferent pupillary defect is an exam finding used in the same acute-neurologic-deficit assessment framework as objective 41.

testable_competencies.exam_interpretation: Perform and interpret the pupillary light reflex, and recognize RAPD (optic nerve/severe retinal disease), pupil-involving vs. pupil-sparing third-nerve palsy (surgical emergency vs. microvascular), and pharmacologic vs. neurologic mydriasis/miosis.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Pupil-involving CN3 palsy substantially overlaps Neurosurgery's compressive-aneurysm objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-exam-finding angle only.

entries.title: Ocular Malignancies (Lid Carcinoma, Uveal Melanoma, Metastases)

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize suspicious lid lesions (basal cell carcinoma -- most common lid malignancy) and pigmented choroidal lesions (uveal melanoma) as requiring biopsy/referral rather than reassurance; no dedicated MCC ocular-oncology objective exists.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Ocular Manifestations of Systemic Infectious and Immune Disease (HIV, Sarcoidosis, Connective Tissue Disease)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Uveitis/scleritis secondary to sarcoidosis or connective tissue disease presents as red eye (see unit 60, Uveitis); no dedicated MCC objective exists for the systemic-disease-to-eye link itself.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize that HIV, sarcoidosis, and connective tissue diseases can produce ocular inflammation (uveitis, scleritis, retinitis) as a presenting or complicating manifestation.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Infectious Diseases/Rheumatology's own disease-specific objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-manifestation angle only.

entries.title: Ocular Manifestations of Diabetes Mellitus (Diabetic Retinopathy)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No dedicated MCC diabetic-retinopathy or diabetes-mellitus objective exists (confirmed via search-mcc-objectives); 130 (Hyperglycemia) is the nearest registry anchor for the underlying systemic disease, per the OB-27 diabetes-in-pregnancy precedent.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of preventable chronic vision loss in working-age adults, within objective 115-2's scope, and drives vitreous hemorrhage risk (unit 31).

testable_competencies.screening: Know the recommended dilated-fundus screening interval for diabetic patients and recognize proliferative retinopathy/macular edema as requiring urgent ophthalmology referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Endocrinology's diabetes-mellitus-complications objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-screening angle only.

entries.title: Ocular Manifestations of Hypertension (Hypertensive Retinopathy)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hypertensive retinopathy is a fundoscopic sign of end-organ hypertensive damage, weakly cross-linking to objective 9-1's target-organ-damage scope; no dedicated ocular objective exists.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize fundoscopic hypertensive retinopathy findings (arteriolar narrowing, AV nicking, flame hemorrhages, papilledema in malignant hypertension) as evidence of end-organ damage.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Cardiology's hypertension-target-organ-damage objective; retained here in thin form for the fundoscopic-sign angle only.

entries.title: Ocular Manifestations of Multiple Sclerosis (Optic Neuritis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Optic neuritis (painful subacute monocular vision loss, often the first presentation of MS) is a direct match to objective 115-1's acute-vision-loss scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize painful subacute monocular vision loss with an afferent pupillary defect as optic neuritis, and know its association with multiple sclerosis, requiring urgent ophthalmology/neurology referral and MRI.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Neurology's multiple sclerosis objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-presentation angle only.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Amaurosis fugax is explicitly named in MCC objective 41's own excerpt ('acute neurological deficits (e.g., aphasia, amaurosis fugax)'), the single most direct evidence citation in this chapter.

testable_competencies.emergency: Recognize transient monocular vision loss (amaurosis fugax) as a TIA-equivalent requiring urgent carotid/cardiac embolic-source workup and stroke-prevention risk-factor management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Thyroid eye disease is a direct ocular manifestation of the thyroid disease covered by objective 63, and is the most common cause of both unilateral and bilateral proptosis in adults.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Severe thyroid eye disease can cause compressive optic neuropathy, an acute-vision-loss emergency within 115-1's scope at WEAK strength given its relative rarity.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize lid retraction, proptosis, and restrictive diplopia as thyroid eye disease, and identify exposure keratopathy or compressive optic neuropathy (sudden vision change) as sight-threatening urgent-referral red flags.

entries.title: Giant Cell (Temporal) Arteritis -- Ocular Manifestations

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: GCA causing sudden, often bilateral, irreversible vision loss (ischemic optic neuropathy) is one of the highest-stakes true ophthalmic emergencies and directly within objective 115-1's scope -- immediate high-dose steroids before biopsy confirmation is the classic teaching point.

testable_competencies.emergency: Recognize GCA red flags (age >50, new headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, sudden vision loss) as requiring immediate empiric high-dose corticosteroids and urgent ESR/CRP plus temporal artery biopsy to prevent irreversible bilateral blindness.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Rheumatology's vasculitis objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-emergency-recognition angle only.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct presentation-level match: MCC objective 102 explicitly requires diagnosing the type/severity/urgency of strabismus and/or amblyopia to prevent irreversible amblyopia.

testable_competencies.screening: Recognize strabismus (misaligned corneal light reflex/cover test) and know that timely referral is essential before the critical period closes, since amblyopia is preventable only with early intervention.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Red-reflex testing to detect leukocoria is part of the periodic well-child examination covered by objective 74's age-specific screening scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize leukocoria (absent red reflex, white pupillary reflex on photograph) as a must-not-miss finding requiring same-week ophthalmology referral to exclude retinoblastoma.

entries.title: Retinopathy of Prematurity

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ROP screening in preterm/low-birth-weight infants is a defined periodic-screening protocol; no dedicated MCC ROP objective exists.

testable_competencies.screening: Know that premature/low-birth-weight infants require scheduled ROP screening examinations to prevent retinal detachment and blindness.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Pediatrics' neonatal-screening objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-screening angle only.

entries.title: Congenital Nasolacrimal Duct Obstruction and Ophthalmia Neonatorum

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Ophthalmia neonatorum is a neonatal red-eye presentation with a distinct infectious differential (chemical, gonococcal, chlamydial) requiring urgent recognition; no dedicated MCC objective exists.

testable_competencies.triage: Distinguish benign congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (tearing, usually resolves by age 1) from ophthalmia neonatorum (purulent neonatal conjunctivitis), which requires urgent evaluation for gonococcal/chlamydial infection given the risk of corneal perforation and systemic spread.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Ophthalmia neonatorum substantially overlaps Pediatrics' neonatal-infection objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-presentation angle only.

entries.title: Congenital Glaucoma

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Congenital glaucoma (buphthalmos, tearing, photophobia, corneal clouding in an infant) is a rare but sight-threatening pediatric cause of vision loss; WEAK link to objective 115-2 given its rarity and specialist-surgical management.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize the infant triad of tearing, photophobia, and blepharospasm with an enlarged, cloudy cornea (buphthalmos) as congenital glaucoma requiring urgent pediatric ophthalmology referral.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match to MCC objective 109's diagnose-cause-severity-complications scope for traumatic injury; penetrating/globe-rupture trauma is a true ophthalmic emergency.

testable_competencies.emergency: Recognize signs of open-globe injury (peaked/irregular pupil, extruded uveal tissue, low IOP, positive Seidel sign) and know that further examination/manipulation is contraindicated -- apply a rigid shield and urgent ophthalmology/OR referral instead.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hyphema (blood in the anterior chamber) is a common traumatic ocular complication with a risk of rebleed and IOP spike, within objective 109's complications scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize traumatic hyphema, know the risk of secondary rebleed and elevated IOP, and manage with activity restriction, upright positioning, and ophthalmology follow-up (avoiding NSAIDs/aspirin).

entries.title: Orbital (Blow-Out) Fracture

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Orbital blow-out fracture is a specific traumatic-complication pattern within objective 109's scope, with a distinctive entrapment/diplopia presentation.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize enophthalmos, restricted upward gaze/vertical diplopia, and infraorbital numbness after blunt periorbital trauma as suggestive of orbital floor fracture, and recognize the 'white-eyed blow-out fracture' in children (muscle entrapment with minimal external signs) as a surgical emergency.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Plastic Surgery/Otolaryngology's facial-fracture objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-presentation angle only.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match to MCC objective 11's severity-diagnosis-and-initial-management scope; ocular chemical burns are the paradigm case requiring immediate action before any history/exam.

testable_competencies.emergency: Recognize ocular chemical exposure (especially alkali, which penetrates faster and deeper than acid) as requiring immediate copious irrigation before any other history, exam, or referral step, and know the litmus-paper/pH-neutralization endpoint for stopping irrigation.

entries.title: Ocular Drug Toxicity

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Drug-induced retinal/corneal toxicity (e.g., hydroxychloroquine maculopathy, amiodarone corneal deposits) causes chronic vision change requiring monitoring; no dedicated MCC ocular-drug-toxicity objective exists, and this content substantially overlaps Clinical Pharmacology's adverse-drug-effect objectives.

testable_competencies.screening: Know which commonly prescribed systemic drugs (hydroxychloroquine, amiodarone, corticosteroids, ethambutol, tamoxifen) require baseline and periodic ophthalmologic monitoring for ocular toxicity.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Clinical Pharmacology's adverse-drug-effect objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-monitoring angle only.

entries.title: Uveitis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Anterior uveitis (iritis) is a vision-threatening cause of painful red eye requiring urgent referral, within objective 30's scope; often associated with HLA-B27 spondyloarthropathy or inflammatory bowel disease.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize anterior uveitis (photophobia, ciliary flush, small/irregular pupil, hypopyon in severe cases) as requiring urgent slit-lamp confirmation and topical cycloplegic/steroid therapy under ophthalmology guidance, and screen for associated systemic inflammatory disease.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Rheumatology/Gastroenterology's HLA-B27-spectrum-disease objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-presentation angle only.

entries.title: Dislocated Lens (Ectopia Lentis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Ectopia lentis is a classic exam finding in Marfan syndrome and homocystinuria, within objective 36's genetic-concerns diagnostic scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize lens dislocation/subluxation as a prompt to evaluate for an underlying genetic connective-tissue or metabolic disorder (Marfan syndrome -- superotemporal dislocation; homocystinuria -- inferonasal dislocation).

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Medical Genetics' Marfan/homocystinuria objectives; retained here in thin form for the ocular-finding angle only.
